2.15   P15: Completion of the unit-volume hypersurface in a background cone
Status: open in the stated generality. Book locator: Problem 32.5.1, printed p. 888.
Setup and scope. Choose a ﬁnite-dimensional real space V of smooth (1, 1)-forms with V ∩
ddc C ∞ (X) = {0}. Let C ⊂ V consist of backgrounds with a smooth positive representative, let
λ = λµ , and put
                         g = −D2 log λ,    S = {θ ∈ C : λ(θ) = 1}.
The distance is the intrinsic Riemannian path distance in this speciﬁed cone or hypersurface.
Full problem statement. For a speciﬁed ﬁnite-dimensional cone of smooth background classes,
describe the metric completion of its unit-volume hypersurface. Which boundary points admit a
current representative, and what estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguish ﬁnite
from inﬁnite distance?
State of the art. Homogeneity gives an isometry (C , g) ≃ (R×S , dr2 +gS ) with r = log λ. Thus
paths with volume tending to zero or inﬁnity have inﬁnite length. The positive cone generated by
the two factors of P1 × P1 is complete in logarithmic coordinates. On the blowup of P2 , a boundary
with positive nef volume can occur at ﬁnite distance.
Remaining gap. Classify Cauchy boundary points of S , their possible current representatives,
and estimates on minimizing metrics distinguishing ﬁnite from inﬁnite distance. Adjoining all nef
classes does not give the answer. Distances may shorten after enlarging the cone, so no conclusion
about the entire inﬁnite-dimensional quotient is implicit.
Sources. Book, Proposition 25.5.1, Example 25.5.1; Chapter 25’s metric geometry section.

unchanged_original_specified_cone_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n, let h be a smooth positive Hermitian form, and let mu be a smooth positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial. For a smooth background theta admitting a smooth positive representative theta+dd^c u, define
D_mu(gamma)=integral_X (mu/gamma^n)^(1/n)gamma^n,
lambda_mu(theta)=inf_gamma [integral_X theta wedge gamma^(n-1)]/D_mu(gamma),
where gamma ranges over smooth positive Hermitian metrics satisfying dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0 (in dimension one lambda is the integral). Put V_mu=lambda_mu^n.
Choose a finite-dimensional real space V of smooth real (1,1) forms with V intersect dd^c C^infinity(X,R)={0}. Let C consist of those backgrounds in V with a smooth positive representative. The smooth positive Hessian metric is g=-D^2 log lambda_mu, restricted to this specified cone or to S={theta in C:lambda_mu(theta)=1}; all distances are their intrinsic Riemannian path distances.
Question: describe the metric completion of the unit-volume hypersurface for a specified geometrically meaningful family of such finite-dimensional cones, identify all Cauchy boundary points and their current representatives, and prove estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguishing finite from infinite distance. Find an explicit nonclosed family beyond the already-known closed two-factor projective cone and blowup-surface example, or establish a more general classification including such a family.
Known background: homogeneity gives (C,g) isometric to R times S with metric dr^2+g_S, r=log lambda. Thus volume tending to zero or infinity forces infinite length. The cone generated by the two closed factors on CP1 times CP1 is complete in logarithmic coordinates, while a boundary with positive nef volume on the blowup of CP2 can occur at finite distance. These examples do not classify other specified cones. Merely adjoining every nef class is not a completion criterion, and enlarging the cone may shorten distances.
This is a precise sufficient-condition classification subtask from the original specified-cone research question. The selected cone must be fully specified and its positivity, absence of smooth dd^c directions and volume formula proved; its complete Cauchy geometry must be established. A proof for that family does not classify arbitrary finite-dimensional nonclosed cones. No candidate family or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_specified_cone_task.completionCriteria: Prove a complete intrinsic metric-completion theorem for a geometrically explicit family including genuinely nonclosed backgrounds. Identify every possible Cauchy boundary point and whether it has a current representative, with rigorous finite/infinite distance estimates tied to the minimizing Gauduchon metrics. Prove the exact volume and Hessian formulas and check any imported metric-geometry statements at primary sources. Keep the specified cone fixed when discussing distance, and distinguish this theorem from a general arbitrary-cone classification. A restatement of the product splitting, of the two closed examples in the question, or of an unproved formal Hessian computation does not suffice. Independently reconstruct the complete proof and check source premises.

current_primary_application_judgment: Parallelizable theorem reconstructs every averaging, determinant, minimizing-metric and matrix distance fact, without nonroutine external premises. Warped theorem imports only smooth interior closed-class Monge-Ampere existence on connected compact Kahler B with strict b*kappa and target (b^m/H)*sigma/L of mass b^m. TW Corollary1 and its full relevant printed proof were previously read and assessed; closed integration removes the scalar and 2pi rescaling gives the stated operator. No endpoint equation or imported metric-completion theorem is used. Its exact full and final review reports were reread this turn. The final task-granted version is retained, while the original primary application is independently checked at unchanged hypotheses.
mathematical_application_judgment: All-test AMGM identifies the genuine full Gauduchon volume and actual attaining metrics. For every fixed invariant subspace W, matrix order lower bounds and normalized chords stay in W and exhaust Cauchy behavior. In warped cones the original affine Hessian, rather than a Hessian of its constant restriction, pulls back to a flat surface. Both endpoint variance laws, separated-annulus lower bounds for critical/infinite ends, arbitrary simultaneous coefficient limits, and positive-current nonbigness tests are complete. No singular current is restricted to a fiber.

clause_assessment.request: Specified nonclosed cones and exact positivity, volume and Hessian
clause_assessment.answer: Every positive invariant-matrix cone in a fixed real linear subspace of a compact complex Lie quotient has lambda=(H det A)^(1/n). An entire three-dimensional warped cone on B times C has V=n b^m/integral sigma/(ca+e). Their positivity cones and absence of dd^c directions are proved from actual tests.

clause_assessment.request: All Cauchy points and current representatives in the specified intrinsic metric
clause_assessment.answer: Invariant slices are complete and proper with coefficient convergence exactly equivalent to intrinsic Cauchy convergence; semipositive coefficient currents add no new unit-volume points. Warped slices are precisely flat open strips, half-planes or planes; all finite faces have displayed smooth semipositive nef nonbig representatives of full volume one.

clause_assessment.request: Finite versus infinite distance estimates tied to minimizing Gauduchon metrics
clause_assessment.answer: Invariant normalized minimizers satisfy two-sided exponential matrix order control, and nonzero singular coefficient limits have logarithmic divergent normalized distance. Warped attaining-metric vertical-trace probabilities give exact reciprocal-coefficient variance. Under finite disjoint power tubes, an extreme end is finite exactly when minimum real-codimension/vanishing-order ratio exceeds one.

clause_assessment.request: Actual nonclosed examples beyond the two known closed examples
clause_assessment.answer: The full non-Kahler Iwasawa cone has explicit determinant, fiber-volume and exact distance constants. The P2 times P1 warped threefold has a finite closed-strip completion with explicit faces 4log2/(3b^2), while a warped elliptic-torus cone has an entire complete plane.

scope_judgment: The original request is for the completion of a specified cone and its current/minimizer boundary criteria. Both geometrically specified families provide complete intrinsic classifications, with finite and infinite cases. The frozen task explicitly distinguishes its sufficient-condition classification from arbitrary-cone classification. The broad book programme stays open; only this exact specified-condition request is counted answered.
